subject: Billing routing and legal-entity split after Everleaf acquisition
messages:
From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@everleaf.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-12-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Upcoming billing split + remit address for Everleaf Labs, LLC

Hi Mina,

Quick note from our finance team — as you may have heard, we closed the acquisition of LeafLabs and are moving a subset of our R&D spend and vendor contracts into the new legal entity, Everleaf Labs, LLC, effective 2027-01-01. Finance would like to: 

- Start routing all R&D-related invoices to Everleaf Labs, LLC (new remit) from 2027-01-01 onwards.
- Keep commercial/product invoices with Everleaf Therapeutics, Inc. (legacy entity).
- Confirm the tax IDs and remit addresses you need so we can provide W-9 / VAT registration documents.

Can you confirm what specific documents and lead time Redwood requires to update invoice routing and tax records? Also let us know if you need us to reissue any open invoices to the new entity.

Attached: Everleaf_Billing_Entity_Change_Form.pdf (fillable)

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
VP Finance (interim)
Everleaf Therapeutics
[sender signature]
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Re: Upcoming billing split + remit address for Everleaf Labs, LLC

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the close. We can support a split routing starting 2027-01-01 but will need a few items to process this cleanly: 

1) Signed W-9 (or equivalent tax certificate) for Everleaf Labs, LLC (new remit).
2) Company legal name, remit address, and tax ID exactly as they should appear on the invoice.
3) Clarification on whether you want us to reissue any invoices dated before 2027-01-01. Reissuing requires approvals from our billing team and may affect collection.

Proposed next steps (we can turn these into a formal amendment if you prefer):
- You upload the filled form + W-9 to the DocuSign/attachments link and reply here.
- We prepare an amendment that (a) splits future invoices by product line codes you provide and (b) updates remit addresses.
- Ben (billing) will confirm the GL mappings and whether back-billing is feasible.

Looping in Ben and Laura to pick up operational and contract items.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Mina / Laura — got it. I sketched a quick checklist for operations: 

- Required docs from customer: W-9 for new entity, copy of Certificate of Formation, signed amendment or PO updates, GL mapping table for R&D vs Commercial spend.
- Implementation options: 
  a) Forward-going split only (cleanest): start invoices 2027-01-01 split by product codes.
  b) Split + reissue historical invoices (only for invoices < 60 days and with customer approval).
- Billing system changes: new remit entity as a customer sub-account; invoices auto-routed based on product code.
- Tax accounting: confirm whether any VAT/withholding applies — looks US-only for now.

I can prepare the sub-account and test invoices once we have the exact remit address and tax ID. If Everleaf prefers, we can run the December 31 billing with the split turned on for R&D items that are forecasted.

Attachments: proposed_split_mapping.csv (stub)

Ben

Ben — this plan looks reasonable. A few legal/contract items to note before we finalize: 

- We need a signed amendment that describes the split rules (which SKUs/line items map to each entity) and confirms indemnities/payment terms remain unchanged.
- If Everleaf requests reissued invoices older than 60 days, route that through revenue ops and finance for approval (possible audit trail/corrections).
- No EU VAT triggers identified today — mark region as US for this thread. If they convert any EU customers or vendors, finance will need notice.

Mina — please request the signed amendment via DocuSign and the W-9. Once we have the signed amendment and W-9, Ben can create the sub-account and adjust routing for the Jan 1 cutover. If Everleaf wants the December 31 run split-applied, tell them there may be a one-time reconciliation on Jan 10.

Laura Bennett
